gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI AC180's ECO auto-off can't be set below 15 W on AC or 5 W on DC. ResMed's table, as Willrun reports it, puts a humidifier-off AirSense 11 at about 7 W, so with ECO on, the AC outlet will cut the CPAP within 1–4 hours, and the 12 V port will too if its threshold is set to 10 W.
standout_why: Pages compared: willitrunpower.com (cited), preparedstates.com (cited), our own dealectric.com page, and ChatGPT's answer. ChatGPT's answer already says to turn off auto power-saving shutdown. Willrun gives Jackery's Energy Saving rule (12 h below 25 W) and EcoFlow's AC timeout, but nothing about the AC180's ECO. Prepared States doesn't mention auto-off at all. Our current page says to turn ECO off and gives 'roughly 10–50 W on other models', with no AC180 figure and nothing on whether the 12 V port is affected. None of them sets the AC180's actual threshold ranges (AC 15–30 W, DC 5–10 W, 1–4 h) against the CPAP's 7 W draw. That comparison shows the AC route fails on every ECO setting, and the DC route survives only at the 5 W setting. The advice to turn auto-off off is already in the rival answers; the exact numbers are new.
decides: The AC180 pick still holds, but this changes how the page should tell people to set it up. A humidifier-off AirSense 11 (about 7 W) on the AC180's AC outlet is under the lowest AC ECO threshold (15 W), so with ECO on, the outlet will switch off within the 1–4 hour window every night. Even with the humidifier on (about 19 W), it stays under the 30 W setting. On the 12 V car port through ResMed's Air11 DC/DC converter, 7 W only stays above the cutoff if the DC threshold is set to 5 W, not 10 W. The page should say to turn ECO off completely (hold AC and DC together to enter settings). If ECO stays on, use the 12 V port with the DC threshold at 5 W. This also backs up the DC route, since it's the only one that can stay on with ECO enabled.

findings.label: ECO mode auto-off thresholds
findings.value: AC output 15–30 W, DC output 5–10 W, for 1, 2, 3 or 4 hours
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 - Portable Power Station Manual (ManualsLib copy of BLUETTI user manual)
findings.note: The manual's FAQ Q4 says: 'You can set the power threshold of AC output and DC output to 15-30W /5-10W, respectively, for 1, 2, 3, or 4 hours.' It also says the outputs 'automatically turn off if the AC180 is bearing low or no load for a while.' This is a copy on a manual-hosting site. BLUETTI's own PDF (cdn.shopify.com/.../AC180_User_Manual.pdf) downloaded, but its text couldn't be extracted. The manual doesn't say whether ECO is on by default.

findings.label: 12 V car outlet rating
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 - Portable Power Station Manual
findings.note: Spec table: 'Cigarette Lighter Port: 12VDC/10A'. That's enough for the Air11 DC/DC converter's 12 V/10 A input rating.

findings.label: ResMed AirSense 11 AutoSet average draw by setting (ResMed power table, as reported by Willrun)
findings.value: 7 W with no humidifier; 19 W with HumidAir 11; 55 W with humidifier and ClimateLineAir 11 heated tube
findings.source_title: Best power station for a CPAP: picks by humidifier, DC vs AC | Willrun
findings.note: Willrun cites ResMed's device power table (resmed-healthcare.de/.../1018528r11_Uebers_Stromverbrauch-Geraete_RDE_PDF-1.pdf). That PDF returned 403 when I tried it, so I'm relying on Willrun's figures. Comparison with the AC180 ECO thresholds: 7 W is below the 15 W AC minimum, so the AC outlet shuts off within 1–4 h with ECO on. 19 W is below the 30 W AC setting. 7 W is above the 5 W DC setting but below the 10 W DC setting. These are averages, so short dips below 5 W are possible.

findings.label: ResMed AirSense 11 65 W power supply consumption (user guide)
findings.value: Typical 56.1 W (111.5 VA), peak 73.2 W (137.6 VA); DC output 24 V ±1 V, 2.71 A
findings.note: The guide doesn't state the measurement conditions. The 56.1 W figure is the supply's rated typical draw, not a humidifier-off draw, so it overstates the dry-night draw.

findings.label: ResMed AirSense 11 DC/DC Converter (part 39231) specs and behaviour
findings.value: Input 12 V/24 V at 10 A/5 A; output 24 V, 3.75 A; works with the HumidAir humidifier and ClimateLineAir heated tube; light turns amber on low battery, and converter and light turn off when the supply is too low
findings.note: UK store, £70 plus VAT. No US price on this page.
